subject: Request: clarification on standby activation window & RTO/RPO exceptions
messages:
From: Samantha Tu <samantha.tu@pecosbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@pecosbank.com>, Pecos Bank Legal <legal@pecosbank.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Clarification on multi-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) and activation window

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we move toward finalizing the procurement paperwork there are a couple of items our compliance and ops teams need clarified about the multi-region failover commitments before we sign:

- Our regulator requires that any customer-controlled switchover in our production environment have a documented minimum activation lead time of 120 minutes for manual approvals and coordinated failover (we can scope out automatic vs manual). Can Redwood accept a carveout that treats manual, operator-initiated failovers as a different SLO class?
- Please confirm the RTO/RPO you guarantee for automated policy-based failover (i.e., when Redwood triggers regional fallback). Separately, what guarantee — if any — would apply for a manual, legally-mandated switchover?
- We need a short runbook (or runbook outline) that shows steps, who acknowledges, and the observable telemetry you’ll provide during switchover for audit purposes.
- Any attachments/annexes you propose for inclusion in an addendum (DocuSign-ready) would be helpful.

Attached: Pecos_SLA_questionnaire_trimmed.pdf (answers pending on a few fields) — the compliance team flagged the manual-activation lead-time requirement specifically.

Can we aim to have a proposed addendum and runbook outline by EOD Monday? If Redwood can’t accept the 120-minute manual carveout, please explain operationally why and what mitigations you can propose.

Thanks —
Samantha Tu
Head of Platform Ops, Pecos Bank
Samantha.Tu@pecosbank.com
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Tu <samantha.tu@pecosbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T11:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) and activation window

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear ask and the questionnaire. We can absolutely work toward a pragmatic addendum that accommodates regulatory constraints while keeping service reliability predictable. High-level answers up front:

- Automated failover (Redwood-initiated policy trigger): standard SLO we commit to is RTO = 15 minutes (time to first response and traffic routing to a healthy region) and RPO = near-zero for supported models when prefix/KV caching is warmed; this assumes the customer is on a dedicated or private tier with pre-configured replication.
- Manual, customer-authorized switchover: Redwood can accept a conditional exception as a separate SLO class (manual-switchover SLO) with an agreed activation lead time. Given your regulator’s 120-minute minimum, we propose an addendum that: 1) designates manual switchover windows separately, 2) defines acceptance tests and telemetry required, and 3) specifies the fallback/rollback commitments post-switchover.

Operational caveats and what we’ll include in the addendum:
- If you require manual confirmation before activation, RTO will be measured from the point of manual authorization — not from incident detection — which will reflect the lead-time.
- For manual scenarios we recommend (and will offer) a pre-warmed standby configuration: reserved GPU pool + KV snapshotting to reduce cold-start effects. If you prefer no pre-warm, we’ll model expected token-latency and cold-cache RTO in the addendum.
- We’ll include a runbook outline (attached) and a proposed SLA addendum draft for your legal review.

Attachments: redwood-proposed-sla-addendum-v0.1.pdf (draft), standby-runbook-outline.txt

Next steps: I’ll sync with our engineering and legal teams (copied) to assess the pre-warm options and expected cost delta; we’ll aim to get a polished addendum and a DocuSign-ready draft by EOD Monday. In the meantime, could you confirm whether Pecos requires guaranteed RPO=0 or whether a tolerable RPO (e.g., <= 60s) for certain model classes is acceptable? That affects snapshot cadence and replication cost.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T13:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) and activation window

Michael / Marissa —

Quick technical note on the manual-activation carveout:

- Cold-start impact: without pre-warmed standby we typically see an additional 8–30 min of latency before throughput stabilizes for long-context models as KV caches populate and kernels settle. That varies by model family and sequence length.
- Pre-warm mitigation: maintaining a warm standby (reserved capacity, periodic KV snapshot replay) can reduce manual-switchover RTO to ~20–30 minutes for large models and <10 minutes for smaller families.
- RPO tradeoffs: to achieve near-zero RPO we’ll need continuous async replication of KV checkpoints. That adds both network and storage overhead; if Pecos is comfortable with a soft RPO (<= 60s) we can reduce replication frequency and cost.

Suggested approach for the addendum:
1) Define two SLO buckets: Automated-Failover (RTO 15m, RPO near-zero with pre-warm) and Manual-Failover (RTO measured from authorization; baseline cold-start model + optional pre-warm).
2) For Manual-Failover, include optional pre-warm as a Billable configuration in the SOW; define expected RTO with and without pre-warm.
3) Include acceptance test matrix (traffic replay for 30 minutes, KV-warm validation, end-to-end latency checks) and the metrics that count toward failure/slash credits.

I can draft the tech annex with expected numbers for Pecos’ sample model if you want.

—Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Tu <samantha.tu@pecosbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Pecos Bank Legal <legal@pecosbank.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T09:01:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) and activation window

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review, Redwood can support the regulator-driven manual-activation lead time as a separate, conditional SLO class. Summary of the agreed approach we propose to put into a DocuSign addendum:

1) Two SLO classes
   - Automated-Failover (default): RTO = 15 minutes; RPO = near-zero for models on dedicated/private tiers with continuous replication and pre-warm enabled.
   - Manual-Failover (customer-authorized): RTO measured from time of customer authorization. Redwood will provide a conservative baseline estimate for cold-start scenarios and a reduced estimate if Pecos elects pre-warm.

2) Activation lead time and measurement
   - If Pecos requires a minimum 120-minute manual-activation lead time for governance reasons, the addendum will record that lead time and state that RTO measurements begin at authorization time (i.e., when Pecos confirms go/no-go).

3) Pre-warm (optional, billable)
   - Offering: Reserved GPU standby with periodic KV replay. With pre-warm we commit to Manual-Failover RTO <= 30 minutes for listed model classes; without pre-warm we’ll publish cold-start RTO ranges (30–120 minutes depending on model size).

4) Acceptance tests, telemetry & auditability
   - We will provide: a runbook outline (attached), a traffic-replay test, KV-warm validation steps, and a telemetry package (per-request traces + token-level latency + switchover timeline) that Pecos can ingest for audit evidence.

5) Cost & timeline
   - Pre-warm reserved capacity will be reflected as a line item in the SOW. Karthik’s team will quantify the expected cost delta after we confirm Pecos’ target model families and QPS.

Attachments included for review: redwood-signed-addendum-draft.pdf (initial wording for legal), standby-runbook-outline.txt

Next steps for Pecos:
- Please confirm whether Pecos requires true RPO=0 or if RPO <= 60s is acceptable for all or some model classes.
- If Pecos accepts the conditional approach, Pecos legal can review the attached draft and we’ll circulate a DocuSign-ready addendum (link below).

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/secure/WTX-488127-addendum-draft
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/20881

If this aligns with your compliance needs we can schedule a 30-min call with Karthik and our legal counsel to walk the acceptance criteria and cost trade-offs.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
